messages:
anna: Running into a weird issue in the Kotlin SDK with release builds (R8/minify=true). When token refresh occurs, OkHttp sends the same request twice and customers reported double billing.

marc: Does it reproduce in debug?

anna: No, only in minified release builds on Pixel and some Samsung devices. Emulator not repro.

olivia: Any proguard rules shipped in the SDK README?

anna: Only basic okhttp keep rules. Adding `-keep class com.redwood.sdk.** { *; }` locally stops the dupes.

marc: That suggests R8 strips something used for dedupe. We tag requests with an internal RequestId class, right?

anna: Yep. `request.tag(RequestId::class.java)` returns null after minification so the auth path thinks it must retry.

olivia: Short term: document a ProGuard snippet. Long term: SDK should add header fallback (X-Redwood-Req-Id) and not rely solely on tag classes.

devops-bot: CI job queued: android-minified-e2e -> #5220

marc: Also add a CI test that builds a minified release and runs the E2E flow triggering refresh. We never had that in CI so regression slipped by.

anna: I'll open RED-2319: sample app PR with proguard rules + SDK change for header fallback + CI test. Tagging @olivia for docs.

olivia: I'll add the ProGuard snippet and migration note to quickstart: recommend upgrading to SDK v1.2.x+ where header fallback exists.

anna: Thanks. For now, I'll include the minimal keep rule in the sample app's proguard-rules.pro as a stopgap.
